# Briony

*Grove Councillor*

|  |  |

## Personality

Merry, gossipy and wiser than she lets on. She prefers to settle disagreements over tea rather than in the Council chamber.

## Lore

Briony is a councillor of the Grove, and she would much rather be in the Herb Gardens. She is sixty-eight, merry, gossipy and a good deal wiser than she lets on, and she has a firm belief that most disagreements in the forest could be settled over a pot of tea in less time than it takes the Council to open its doors. She is usually right. Half the forest's quarrels reach the bench beside Hesper's potting shed before they reach the Heart Tree, and a fair number never go any further.

### The gardens and the school

Briony grew up in the forest with her older sister Thessaly, two girls who could not have been less alike: Thessaly precise and proud and always right, Briony cheerful and untidy and always talking. At twelve Briony was sent to the Herb Gardens to learn plants under old Mistress Yarrow, and in her second year a new weeding girl arrived, fifteen, blunt and smelling of mint even then. That was Hesper. They have been friends ever since, more than half a century now, and Briony still says Hesper is the only person who has ever told her to be quiet and made it stick.

Briony did not stay in the gardens. She had a gift for talking, which Yarrow said was wasted on lettuces, and at twenty-seven she went up to the Grove School to teach herb-lore. She taught it there for thirty-six years: which leaf soothes and which leaf blisters, how to tell a healing mushroom from its poisonous cousin, and why you should never trust anyone who says a plant is harmless. Generations of the forest's children learned their first herbs from her, mostly through stories about people who had eaten the wrong thing. Five years ago she gave up the classroom and took a seat on the Grove Council, and she has spent those five years finding excuses to be somewhere else.

### Her sister

Thessaly, her sister, is a councillor too, the one who keeps a ledger of every promise the Council makes and objects to almost everything before agreeing to it. When the elders chose their Eldest nine years ago, Thessaly lost to Calyra by a handful of voices. Briony was the only person who knew how much that cost her, and the only person Thessaly let see it.

In the Council chamber the sisters often take opposite sides, and Briony is the only person who can make Thessaly laugh in the middle of a meeting. She does it on purpose, usually when a debate has gone sour, with a remark nobody else quite hears. Thessaly then has to cover her mouth with her ledger, and the meeting goes better afterwards. Briony thinks of it as a public service. Thessaly has asked her to stop more than once, and does not mean it.

### The bench by the shed

Most days, Briony is in the Herb Gardens, on the bench beside Hesper's potting shed, with a cup of tea and a basket of something that needs sorting. Hesper works; Briony talks; between them, the forest's affairs are settled long before the Council hears of them. Briony hears everything: which seal scholars have stopped sleeping, which apprentice has broken another lantern, which couple has quarrelled, and what Celandine really thinks about the plant at the Forest Edge. She repeats most of it, cheerfully, to anyone who sits down. The things that matter she repeats to no one.

Lately she has noticed Hesper writing in the back of her seed book, late in the day, with a face Briony has not seen on her in fifty years. Briony has not asked what it is. She knows Hesper will tell her when she is ready, and she knows, too, that Hesper has not yet shown it to anyone at the Heart Tree. She has been wondering, quietly, whether a councillor who sits on the bench by the shed ought to be the one to carry it up the stair.

### What she wants and fears

Briony wants the Council to do less talking and more listening, and she wants her sister to laugh more often outside it. She fears, though she hides it behind gossip, that the forest's troubles are growing faster than tea can settle them.

A quest might ask a traveller to carry a pot of tea and a carefully chosen piece of news between Briony and Thessaly, to help her settle a quarrel between two families before it reaches the Council, or to find out what Hesper is writing in the back of her seed book.
